The area of a circular oil spill starts from zero and grows at a constant rate of $12\pi {\text{ m}}^{2}\text{/s}.$ Determine the length of the radius at the moment when it is increasing at a rate of $3\text{ m/s}.$

$r=$
{{field-1}} $\text{m}$
feedback.worked_solution:
In this situation, we want to find $r$ at the moment when $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=3,$ and we are also told that  $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=12\pi .$

To start, let's write down the area formula for the circle and then differentiate it using implicit differentiation. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\pi {r}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\pi {r}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}r}(\pi {r}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2\pi r.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=12\pi $ and $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=3,$ and solve for $r.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}12\pi  & =3\cdot 2\pi r \\ 12\pi  & =6\pi r \\ r & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the radius at that moment is $2\text{ m}.$
